end.summary:
Ishaan classified decimals as terminating, repeating, or non-repeating across 6 attempts, with 3 unaided correct.
They identified 0.375 as terminating and recognised repeating patterns such as 0.333… and 0.777… as rational.
They converted 0.555… to 5/9 and 0.777… to 7/9; for 0.2727… they reduced 27/99 to 3/11.
They used the multiplication-and-subtraction method for 0.1666… and obtained 1/6.
The misconception that every non-ending decimal is irrational was seen twice and corrected by the end of the lesson; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Ishaan practised classifying decimals and converting repeating decimals into fractions. They used repeating patterns, fraction reduction, and the multiplication-and-subtraction method; they also identified that 7/20 terminates because its denominator has only factors 2 and 5. There was an initial mix-up that every non-ending decimal is irrational, but they corrected it later by distinguishing repeating decimals from non-repeating ones. At home, ask them to sort a few decimals into terminating, repeating, and non-repeating groups and explain why each group belongs there.
